newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Electronics push Taiwan stocks to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Electronics push Taiwan stocks to higher close.

text.p: A dramatic rebound by Taiwan's trendsetting electronics sector sent share prices surging sharply on Thursday, helping the index recover better than half of what it lost in a two-day, 450-point tumble, brokers said.
The benchmark index was propelled higher by Wall Street's technology issue-driven rally and aggressive bargain hunting, with investors buying heavily on electronics, brokers said.
As electronics moved ever higher, the weighted index rose through the day to close at 9,632.42, a gain of 251.36 points or 2.68 percent compared to Wednesday's 9,381.06 close.
At T$150.9 billion, turnover was strong but well below the T$200 billion-plus levels seen almost daily in recent weeks.
Analysts said the reduced turnover was likely to come as a relief to financial authorities known to be worried that loose money-market liquidity was fuelling this year's huge rally.
"This kind of turnover will be seen as reasonable," said Lin Long-hsien, assistant manager of United Securities.

The central bank has taken repeated measures to soak up liquidity and in turn cool stock turnover that soared to a historic high T$296.8 billion on July 17 as the red-hot bourse siphoned funds out of the banking system.
"After the sharp falls in the past two sessions, a technical rebound is not surprising," Lin said.
He said recent Wall Street and Nasdaq composite rallies also helped to stir Taiwan's bullish mood.

Bellwether electronics, fuelled by strong fundementals, chalked up an impressive 6.56 percent gain. Before Thursday the sector had been hit sharply by profit-taking and had plunged more than 15 percent since last Thursday.
Chipmaker United Microelectronics rose to the seven-percent daily limit shortly after the market opened, and maintained that gain to close T$7.50 higher at T$120.
